_readme: Access + facts cache for the book-log / book-suggest skills. Machine-maintained, fully regenerable — delete any entry and the next run re-derives it. Keeps book-recommendations.md from carrying link-laden Access cells that go stale silently (the Mistborn 2026-08-26 lesson). AUTHORITATIVE for access: when this file and book-recommendations.md disagree, this file wins and the notes get fixed.
_supersededProfileRev: Was a single date, bumped on any rule change, which invalidated every cached judgement at once. Replaced 2026-08-26 by per-dependency counters in book-revs.json: a rule change now invalidates only the estimates that recorded that rule as a dep, and /book-log recomputes exactly those. This file holds dated facts about the world, invalidated by time passing, not by a rule moving. The one exception is the `occultCheck` blocks, which are judgements kept here for their provenance; they stay valid because axis:occult is a mandatory dep on every line of book-estimates.jsonl, so a change to the occult rule re-examines every book regardless.

_ttlDays._note: enAudio.verified means the *search* need not be redone for 30 days, but every link must still be liveness-checked before it is handed to the reader. enAudio.none is deliberately short: Mistborn's 'none' went stale in 4 days.

_states: verified | none | doubtful (a route exists but is abridged, AI-narrated or below ~60% of published runtime) | unchecked

flags: Not to be confused with The Exterminator (1960), the earlier cut-up collaboration with Brion Gysin.
Early editions were subtitled a novel although the book is a collection.
Several pieces first appeared in Rolling Stone, the Village Voice, Evergreen Review and Esquire.

books.title: Ilustrado
books.author: Miguel Syjuco
flags: The death is investigated, but the satisfaction on offer is the portrait of the Philippines rather than the identity of a culprit - an investigation-shaped frame, not a detective novel.
The author writes himself into the book under his own name; the excerpted works of Crispin Salvador are invented.

books.title: In the Lives of Puppets
books.author: TJ Klune

cz.note: English-language Tor edition, not a Czech translation - the record carries no translator and the catalogue keyword is 'anglictina'. flags: The catalogue holding is the English-language Tor edition, not a Czech translation; the record's keywords list angličtina.
A science-fiction retelling of Pinocchio, hitting the classic's beats including the inventor, the circus man and a Blue Fairy analogue.
Contains brief body horror (a bone protruding from the protagonist's arm in an early flashback).
Reviewers read Victor as asexual and as neurodivergent without either being stated in the text; that is interpretation, not authorial statement.

books.title: Invader
books.author: Simon Scarrow, T. J. Andrews
flags: Originally published as five e-book novellas and collected as one volume of 369 pages (Headline, 2016); reviewers say the seams show in the pacing.
Figulus is a supporting character carried over from Scarrow's Eagles of the Empire series, where he served with Macro and Cato; here he leads.
Czech edition BB/art 2019, transl. Jitka Fialova; original title Invader.

books.title: Jak se vaří drak
books.author: Václav Dvořák
flags: Self-published; illustrated by Jakub Cenkl, who is credited as co-author in some catalogues.
The author has twice won the Magnesia Litera readers' award, for other books.

books.title: Kamzíkův velký skok
books.author: Daniel Rušar
flags: A 40-page illustrated picture book, illustrated by Ľuboslav Paľo, aimed primarily at preschool children.
Marketed as a methodical aid for parents and kindergartens; the procedure for telling a child about a death was checked with a psychologist.
Reported out of print at Czech retailers.

books.title: All Who Go Do Not Return
books.author: Shulem Deen
flags: Won the 2015 National Jewish Book Award.
The author wrote the pseudonymous blog 'Hasidic Rebel' while still inside the community.

books.title: Kdo zastavi dest
books.author: Helena Zakova
flags: The author's first novel, about 518 pages; her later title is Saudade.
Written in Czech, so no translation is involved.

books.title: The House of Gucci
books.author: Sara Gay Fordenová
flags: Non-fiction reportage, not a novel. The author was Milan bureau chief for Women's Wear Daily, covered the trial in court and corresponded with Reggiani in prison.
Original The House of Gucci (2000), with a new epilogue in 2001 and a new afterword in 2021; Czech edition Barecz & Conrad Books 2022, transl. Vladan Sir.
The catalogue signal flagged 'detective'. The true-crime frame is real but the culprit is established history, so the book is not an investigation.

books.title: Kniha o tichu
books.author: Josef Formanek
flags: Illustrated by Dalibor Nesnidal.
A later Gekko printing appeared in 2021.

books.title: The Book of Lost Names
books.author: Kristin Harmel
flags: The reader has already excluded another Harmel standalone, Vinařova žena (The Winemaker's Wife), on axis:infidelity; the two books share no characters, plot or setting and this one is not a sequel to it.
Sources disagree on the year of the present-day frame, 1986 or 2005.
Based on real Resistance document forgers, including Adolfo Kaminsky and Alice Cohn.

books.title: Colossus
books.author: Colin Falconer
flags: Alternate history: the book departs from the record at Alexander's death.
Published in the US as Colossus (St Martin's Press 2015) and later revised for the author's Epic Adventure series; the Czech BB/art 2015 translation follows the earlier text.

books.title: The Queen of Paris
books.author: Pamela Binnings Ewenová
flags: Original title The Queen of Paris: A Novel of Coco Chanel (Blackstone, 2020); Czech edition Ceska citadela 2020, transl. Stanislav Pavlicek.
Publisher frames it as fiction based on facts, some uncovered only recently; the Spatz (Hans Gunther von Dincklage) thread appears mainly as an espionage subplot in the material available.

books.title: The Queen's Lender
books.author: Jean Findlay
flags: Hardback runs 201 pages (Scotland Street Press, 2022); listed as the first of a Queens of Europe sequence.
Czech edition Bourdon 2024, transl. Denis Molcanov; original title The Queen's Lender.
Readers have challenged some historical detail (Buckingham's origins, an anachronistic reference to Covenanters).

books.title: Krev budoucnosti
books.author: Samuel Hornek
flags: Databaze knih records the publication year as 2020 rather than 2019; the catalogue record gives 2019.
The author's debut; no professional reviews found.

books.title: Kronika zlatých časů
books.author: Zdeněk Volný
flags: 288 pages, hardcover, Via Facti 2010.
Rated 70% by genre readers on Legie.info, below the same author's Oko chimery at 85%.
No professional reviews found.

books.title: The Legend of Broken
books.author: Caleb Carr
flags: The Czech edition is a translation of the full text; the framing includes invented Gibbon-Burke letters and a large body of endnotes.
The same author's Alienist novels are detective fiction; this book is not one of them, though it carries a plague-investigation thread.

books.title: Louceni s Jeruzalemem
books.author: Viktor Fischl
flags: Melantrich 1997; written in Czech by an author who lived in Israel under the name Avigdor Dagan.
The publisher's annotation names 'tajemstvi vestby' - a divination or fortune-telling motif - which the occult axis would need to examine.
No full literary review of this title surfaced; the critical characterisation used here is the Slovnik ceske literatury entry on the author's prose, which discusses this novel by name.
Another book by this author, Pata ctvrt, is already excluded on a detective heading; it is an unrelated standalone, not a predecessor of this one.

books.title: The Huntress
books.author: Kate Quinn
flags: Three points of view across pre-war, wartime and post-war timelines.
Content includes the murder of children.
The author's note documents the real Night Witches regiment and post-war Nazi hunting.

books.title: Matrjoška
books.author: Josef Farkas
flags: Short - readers describe it as an afternoon's reading, with large type.
Readers describe the ending as strange and left open.

books.title: Moonshadow
books.author: J. M. DeMatteis, Jon J. Muth
flags: This is a comics work, not prose - widely described as the first fully painted American graphic novel; the Czech edition is the original work, not an adaptation of a novel.
Originally 1985 from Marvel Epic, later reissued by Vertigo with a coda one-shot, Farewell, Moonshadow, and collected as The Compleat Moonshadow.
Art is by Jon J. Muth with George Pratt and Kent Williams assisting.

books.title: City of Promise
books.author: Beverly Swerlingová
flags: Fourth in Swerling's Old New York sequence, after City of Dreams, City of Glory and City of God; readers disagree on whether it stands alone.
Original title City of Promise: A Novel of New York's Gilded Age (2011); Czech edition BB/art 2012, transl. Gerik Cisar.

books.title: Cloud Cuckoo Land
books.author: Anthony Doerr
flags: Original title Cloud Cuckoo Land (2021), about 620 pages; Czech edition MOBA 2022, transl. Blanka Sustrova.

Chapters rotate between six main characters over five timelines in anachronic order, interleaved with fragments of the invented Antonius Diogenes text; the novel is bookended by the generation-ship thread.

books.title: Milenci v roce 2042
books.author: Ladislav Chrudina
flags: Essentially no reception: a single rating on CBDB and no readable reviews found.
The author writes mainly outside SF - a debut set on a Croatian island, a historical novel about Adriatic uskoks, and a children's book.

books.title: Moriandr
books.author: Martina Grmolenská
flags: Illustrated children's book for ages 8-10, typeset to be dyslexia-friendly; funded by a Hithit crowdfunding campaign that closed in November 2020.
The catalogue records no publisher; the author self-published.
Publication year is ambiguous - the campaign closed in 2020 and the author's own site tags the book 2022.

books.title: Mosty přes propast času
books.author: Ludmila Vaňková
flags: An omnibus of two novels, Zeme muj domov and Cas carodeju.
First published 1977 by Mlada fronta; further editions 1992, 2006 and 2020.
The 2020 edition is a single heavy volume - readers report it is physically hard to hold.
Male characters are designated T1 to T50 and female characters by R numbers; readers report this makes them harder rather than easier to tell apart.

books.title: You Had Me at Hello
books.author: Mhairi McFarlane
flags: Present-day chapters alternate with university flashbacks.
Two further adultery threads: a friend discovers her husband's affair, and the lead's fiance had cheated before proposing.
Occult status unexamined at this exit.

books.title: Ghost Boy
books.author: Martin Pistorius a Megan Lloyd Davies
flags: Co-written with the ghostwriter Megan Lloyd Davies.
Contains sustained accounts of physical and sexual abuse by carers.
Published in English as Ghost Boy: The Story of My Locked-in Life (UK/South Africa) and Ghost Boy: The Miraculous Escape of a Misdiagnosed Boy Trapped Inside His Own Body (US).
Czech translation Prah 2016, prel. Jana Jasova.

books.title: Něco úžasného
books.author: Jan Liška
flags: No reader or critical reviews of this title were found; the description rests on publisher and retailer copy.

books.title: Innocence
books.author: Dean Koontz
flags: The US edition carries a bonus short story, Wilderness, covering Addison's childhood; the Czech edition's contents were not checked.
Contains an investigation-shaped thread - Gwyneth pursuing her father's killer - but the culprit is known to the reader, so the satisfaction is not whodunnit.
The supernatural Fogs and Clears are ambient presences; no rite is performed by any character on the page.

books.title: Nightbirds
books.author: Kate J. Armstrong
flags: First of a series; a second volume exists.
Marketed as young adult; the clients-by-night framing sits close to a courtesan setting without the plot being sexual.

books.title: Mathias Sandorf
books.author: Jules Verne
flags: The Albatros 2010 holding is Ondrej Neff's modern retelling, illustrated by Zdenek Burian - an adaptation, not a translation of Verne's text.
Verne's original is 'Mathias Sandorf' (1885); unabridged Czech translations exist under the title 'Matyas Sandorf'.
cz.state on the task line is 'unchecked' and carries no record id.

books.title: Nový věk
books.author: Egon Bondy
flags: The Akropolis 2017 volume pairs two separate works, Nový věk (1982) and Nepovídka (1983); Nepovídka is a long prose text mixing science fiction, anti-utopia and philosophical treatise, and is a different book from the one estimated here.
Both first circulated in samizdat and in the exile journal Svědectví; this is the first textually revised book edition, with an afterword by Martin Machovec.
One reference work dates Nový věk to the first century rather than the seventeenth; the sources conflict.

books.title: Seed to Dust: A Gardener's Story
books.author: Marc Hamer
flags: Published in the UK as Seed to Dust: A Gardener's Story and in North America as Seed to Dust: Life, Nature, and a Country Garden.
Czech translation Kazda 2021, prel. Vojtech Ettler.

books.title: Ostrov ztracenych snu
books.author: Tamara McKinley
flags: The author writes Australian family sagas; the catalogue records this as part of the Klokan series.

books.title: Personal Recollections of Joan of Arc
books.author: Mark Twain
flags: Twain published it pseudonymously as a translation of a memoir by the Sieur Louis de Conte; the framing is stated in a short preface and does not fragment the narrative.
Structured in three parts - childhood, campaign, trial.

books.title: Po stopach ztraceneho syna
books.author: Petr Hugo Slik
flags: Third of a four-book Klarov series (Tajemstvi jeskyne pokladu 2015, Ve stare cihelne se sviti 2017, this 2018, Zahada dracino klice 2019); the Czech catalogue records the 2020 printing.
Catalogue heading is dobrodruzne pribehy - a children's adventure, not literary fiction in the adult sense; genre recorded as litfic only because the book has no speculative element.
Marketed in the tradition of Jaroslav Foglar's Stinadla books.
The catalogue record gives no verified Czech print holding (cz.state unchecked).

books.title: Pohadka z hnizda
books.author: Irena Riclova Lachoutova
flags: Published in the Cteni pro prvnacky (Reading for First-Graders) edition - illustrated, for children just starting to read.
Bambook is a Grada imprint; the author also illustrates.
The catalogue record gives no verified Czech print holding (cz.state unchecked).

books.title: Popletene pocitani
books.author: Veronika Zacharova & Stepanka Sekaninova
flags: Fourteen pages, board/leporelo format with a ring binding, published as educational rather than fiction; the author of record is Stepanka Sekaninova with illustrations by Veronika Zacharova.
The catalogue record gives no verified Czech print holding (cz.state unchecked).

books.title: The First Time
books.author: Joy Fielding
flags: The task line named a separate already-excluded standalone by this author, Spatna dcera, on a detective filter; the two books share no series and no characters.
Narration alternates between three points of view: the wife, the husband and the daughter.

books.title: Battle Flag
books.author: Bernard Cornwell
flags: Third of four volumes in the Starbuck Chronicles; the preceding volumes set up the Starbuck-Faulconer feud that drives this one.
The author's Saxon Stories sequence is excluded on the occult filter; that is a different series and this book does not depend on it.
Readers report a pronounced Confederate sympathy in the portrayal, with Northern characters and commanders drawn flatter.

books.title: Der Junge im Schrank: Eine Kindheit im Krieg
books.author: Senek Rosenblum
flags: Written in German ('Der Junge im Schrank', 2009); the Czech translation is from the German, not from Polish.
Czech subtitle: 'Chlapec ve skrini'.
Occult status unexamined at this exit.

books.title: The Biafra Story: The Making of an African Legend
books.author: Frederick Forsyth
flags: Forsyth's debut; a revised edition was published in 1977 after the war ended, and later editions carry the subtitle The Making of an African Legend.
Forsyth left the BBC in 1968 amid accusations of bias toward the Biafran cause; the book is openly partisan and its factual claims about British involvement remain contested in the historiography.

books.title: The Midnight Rose
books.author: Lucinda Riley
flags: Reviewers describe the heroine as having second sight and the book as carrying a ghost-story strand; that content was not examined at this exit.

books.title: The Religion
books.author: Tim Willocks
flags: First of a Tannhauser trilogy.
Czech translation BB/art 2008, prel. Eva Kristkova.

books.title: Rebel
books.author: Bernard Cornwell
flags: The Starbuck Chronicles run to four volumes and the sequence was never finished by the author.
The author's Saxon Stories sequence (Posledni kralovstvi, Bledy jezdec, Pohansky pan) is excluded on the occult filter; that is a different series and this book does not depend on it.

books.title: Révi a Město snů
books.author: Veronika Hurdová
flags: 393 pages; an audiobook read by Matous Ruml and Tereza Rumlova also exists.
Retailers describe the audience inconsistently - some as 10+, while the protagonists are 15 to 19.
Reviewers draw an explicit comparison to Orwell's 1984.

books.title: RobotiCS
books.author: Tomáš Cícha
flags: Czech original, the author's first novel.
Illustrated by Michal Rumlena.
Sold as part of a franchise with a tie-in strategic card game (robotics-world.net).

books.title: Sesterstvo a sila moci
books.author: Lucie Hlavinkova
flags: Fifth volume of the series; the cast and the magic cat are established in the earlier books.
Albatros 2022, roughly 144 pages, marketed from age 10.
The catalogue record gives no verified Czech print holding (cz.state unchecked).

books.title: The Titanic Sisters
books.author: Patricia Falvey
flags: Sources disagree on which sister assumes which identity after the sinking; publisher copy and Publishers Weekly differ.
Publishers Weekly reports a sexual-predator thread in one sister's new household.
The author has written five Ireland-set novels, including The Yellow House and The Famine Orphans.

books.title: Severka
books.author: Nina Špitálníková
flags: The author's first novel; she previously published the non-fiction Mezi dvěma Kimy and Svědectví o životě v KLDR, the latter a Magnesia Litera winner.
Built from the story of one of the defectors she interviewed for that book.
Opens with a short omniscient prologue before switching to first person.

books.title: The Siberia Job
books.author: Josh Haven
flags: English title is The Siberia Job, not The Siberian Job; Czech edition Bourdon 2024, transl. Jan Skrob.
Marketed as inspired by real events; reviewers identify Fort Worth investor John Kleinheinz as the model for the lead and as an uncredited source, which the book itself does not acknowledge.
Only reader reviews were available - no professional criticism surfaced.

books.title: A Mad Desire to Dance
books.author: Elie Wiesel
flags: Original French title Un desir fou de danser (2006); English A Mad Desire to Dance (2009). Czech edition Portal 2007, transl. Alena Blahova.
Doriel believes himself possessed by a dybbuk, a figure from real Jewish folk occultism; whether any rite is performed on the page was not examined at this exit.

books.title: The Glassmaker
books.author: Tracy Chevalier
flags: The narrative uses a deliberate time-slip: the characters age slowly while external history runs from 1486 to the 2020s.
The real Murano beadmaker Marietta Barovier appears as a mentor figure.
Czech translation Kazda 2025, prel. Karolina Snajdrova.

books.title: Soví příběh
books.author: Kamila Ulčová
flags: Large-format illustrated book, 204 pages at 24 x 31.5 cm; the author is also the illustrator.
First edition listed as sold out at major Czech retailers.
Filed by one retailer as fairy tales and legends for readers 10+.

books.title: Starostliva veverka
books.author: Zuzana Pospisilova
flags: Fragment 2020, 126 pages, illustrated by Zuzana Slanska; part of a Czech-authored series marketed as based on true events.
The catalogue record gives no verified Czech print holding (cz.state unchecked).

books.title: Statecny cap
books.author: Jana Olivova
flags: Fragment 2020, 128 pages, illustrated by Zuzana Slanska, marketed from age 8 as a two-to-three-hour read; fourth in the series.
The catalogue record gives no verified Czech print holding (cz.state unchecked).

books.title: Masha and the Bear: Spooky Stories
books.author: překlad Roman Sikora
flags: A translated media tie-in: the original is Masha and the Bear - Spooky Stories, translated from English by Roman Sikora; the catalogue lists the translator in the author field and no author is credited.
128 pages, Egmont 2022, age 4+, glow-in-the-dark cover.
The Czech route is unchecked in the catalogue record: no recordId and no edition type were resolved.
A different Czech book by Štěpánka Sekaninová shares the title Strach má velké oči and is unrelated to this one.

books.title: Disney: Spooky Stories
books.author: překlad Roman Sikora
flags: A translated licensed tie-in: original Disney compilation, credited to a collective of authors, translated by Roman Sikora; the catalogue lists the translator in the author field.
Egmont 2022, hardback, with an e-book edition also published.
The Czech route is unchecked in the catalogue record: no recordId and no edition type were resolved.
The contents are retellings of Disney film properties, not the original works by Kipling, Milne or Barrie.

books.title: Remembrance
books.author: Danielle Steel
flags: An earlier Czech edition of the same translation appeared from Ikar in 2000; the 2015 printing is a reissue.
Filmed as a television adaptation whose plot differs from the novel.

books.title: Svedectvi o zivote v KLDR
books.author: Nina Spitalnikova
flags: The catalogue also holds an audio edition: OneHotBook 2021, partly read by the author.
A second volume exists ('Svedectvi o zivote v KLDR 2'), with eight further interviews, some continuing speakers from this one.
The catalogue's genre/form heading lists audiobooks and CDs; cz confirms the print holding.

books.title: The Light After the War
books.author: Anita Abriel
flags: Inspired by the author's mother's wartime survival.
Sources disagree on the name of one of the later love interests.

books.title: A Bend in the Stars
books.author: Rachel Barenbaum
flags: The novel alternates between two travelling groups after the opening.
One review's account of the ending, including the survival of the soldier and the birth of the child, comes from a single blog and is not corroborated by a major outlet.

books.title: When She Returned
books.author: Lucinda Berry
flags: Original title When She Returned; the author's The Perfect Child was published in Czech as Andílek (Ikar 2020).
Three narrators.
The author is a clinical psychologist who researched childhood trauma.

books.title: In Another Time
books.author: Jillian Cantor
flags: Two alternating first-person narrators in separate decades.
Frequently compared by reviewers to The Time Traveler's Wife.

books.title: Vabeni mesice
books.author: Petra Kvasnickova
flags: Czech original, not a translation; the author's debut, published by Pointa (2021), 272 pages.
Reader reviews on Databaze knih report the text as effectively unedited.

books.title: Valentynka a narozeniny
books.author: Ivana Peroutkova
flags: First volume of the Valentynka series (Albatros 2018, 120 pages); the sequel is Valentynka a daleke kraje, 2019, marketed from age 7.
An Albatros audiobook of about two hours exists.
The catalogue record gives no verified Czech print holding (cz.state unchecked).

books.title: Válka o přežití lidské rasy
books.author: David Kühn
flags: 276 pages, Powerprint 2020; the author's debut, apparently subsidy-published.
Several reader reviews independently note poor proofreading.
No literary-press coverage found.

books.title: Válka skončila na Hané
books.author: Vilém Sacher
flags: Published posthumously; the manuscript was returned to the author by publishers in the early 1970s and only appeared in 2012.
Chronologically follows the author's Krvavé velikonoce.
The author was a lieutenant general and a Charter 77 signatory, stripped of rank and decorations after signing.

books.title: The Bee Sting
books.author: Paul Murray
flags: Shortlisted for the 2023 Booker Prize.
Around 640 pages; Imelda's section is narrated without punctuation.
Czech translation Akropolis 2025, prel. Lukas Novak.

books.title: Jake Ransom and the Howling Sphinx
books.author: James Rollins
flags: Second book of the Jake Ransom series; it continues directly from Jake Ransom and the Skull King's Shadow, where Calypsos, the Skull King and the parents' disappearance are established, so it does not stand alone.
The series was left unfinished and this book ends on a cliffhanger that was never resolved.
Reviewed as grades 5-9 / ages 8-12.

books.title: A Great Love of Small Proportion
books.author: Colin Falconer
flags: Also published as Converso (revised edition, with additional scenes); the earlier text appeared as A Great Love of Small Proportion, which is what the Czech BB/art 2018 edition renders.
Character names differ between editions - the painter is Diego Sanchis in the earliest version, and the heroine is Mencia in some editions and Mercedes in others.

books.title: Vítek, křupadlo a kostižrout
books.author: Petula Bendula
flags: A gamebook, not a linear novel: 400 pages, 999 game positions, 65 endings; form recorded as novel because the schema has no gamebook value.
Petula Bendula is a pen name for Lucie Nemcova; self-published.
Marketed for readers aged 9-12 and for parents to play along.

books.title: Survival in the Killing Fields
books.author: Haing Ngor, Roger Warner
flags: Co-written with Roger Warner, who shaped the narrator's English into continuous prose.
Later editions add an epilogue by Warner on the author's last years and his unsolved murder in 1996.

books.title: The View Across the Rooftops
books.author: Suzanne Kelman
flags: Originally published by Bookouture, 2019.
The catalogue holds a second print copy of the same edition: MOBA 2021, translated by Michaela Teličková.
A side thread follows the professor's niece Ingrid.

books.title: Zazemi
books.author: Jana Sramkova
flags: The author's second book, following the Jiri Orten Prize-winning novella Hruskadottir.
Written in Czech, so no translation is involved.

books.title: Židle pro Anhelinu
books.author: Ivona Březinová
flags: About 88 pages, hardback, illustrated by Veronika Šporclová; published by Albatros in the Má to háček line, made with Pasparta.
The Czech route is unchecked in the catalogue record: no recordId and no edition type were resolved.
Other titles in the same line handle shared custody, bullying and childhood diabetes, so the format is an issue book rather than free-standing fiction.

books.title: River Thieves
books.author: Michael Crummey
flags: Based on real events and real figures - David Buchan, the Peytons, and the Beothuk woman known as Demasduit; some characters are invented.
Told from four alternating viewpoints on a non-linear timeline.
Czech translation Akropolis 2023, prel. Jiri Kanak.

books.title: Are You Proud of Me, Joanna?
books.author: Janne Teller
flags: Written in English as Are You Proud of Me, Joanna? (2024), published first in Danish; Czech edition Pulchra 2025, transl. Karla Korteova, 320 pages. Spanish edition titled Justicia.
The author worked as a UN and EU diplomat and began the book while doing so; it is her first novel in eleven years, after Nothing (Intet).
Could not source how the novel opens or how many timelines are live by the end of chapter one; the sole substantial review says the narrative spans interwoven timelines across nearly half the planet.
Set against the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

books.title: To Lie with Lions
books.author: Dorothy Dunnettová
flags: Sixth of eight in Dorothy Dunnett's House of Niccolo; original title To Lie with Lions (1995). Not a standalone entry point.
Czech edition BB/art 2012, transl. Lucie Johnova.
Only publisher copy and reader reviews were available; no professional criticism surfaced.

books.title: Úder tornáda
books.author: Ivona Březinová
flags: Eighth instalment of the GO! - Gang odvážných series; 112 pages, illustrated by Matyáš Namai, Albatros 2022.
The Czech route is unchecked in the catalogue record: no recordId and no edition type were resolved.
Rated below the series average on Databáze knih (73 percent against 86 percent for the preceding instalment).

books.title: The Eagle's Conquest
books.author: Simon Scarrow
flags: Second book of the Eagles of the Empire series; it opens immediately after the events of Under the Eagle and assumes both leads are already known.
The series runs to more than twenty volumes.
Czech translation BB/art 2010, prel. Ludmila Havlikova a Tomas Havlik.

lessons: The broad category terms are near-useless as-is: 'vzpominky' and 'biografie' are ~2000 records each of mostly Czech celebrity and local-history memoir. Targeted theme AND queries (Ujgur, islam autobiografie, Severni Korea) yielded far more per request than any full-category pull.

'svedectvi' (521) is dominated by Holocaust and communism testimony. That is the Anne Frank 40 form, which failed outright — so a hit in this category is NOT automatically a Qureshi 91 analogue. What earns is examined truth plus another group's lived experience, and contemporary contested subjects (Xinjiang, apostasy, North Korea) match it far better than the historical canon does.

Alegorie + podobenstvi + filozoficka proza together are only 105 records — the single cheapest slice in the catalogue to screen exhaustively, and it maps onto the log's safest category. Should have been done first.
flags: Kacířka (Heretic) by Hirsi Ali is argument rather than memoir — brushes the no-apologetics-as-subject line. Propose Rebelka (Infidel) instead. Same distinction already recorded for Qureshi.

sweeps.label: Short-story screen, exhaustive
sweeps.method: Two passes over the same set: (1) match against a target list of ~50 canonical idea-driven short-fiction authors; (2) rank all authors whose records sit on an adult imprint (Triton, Laser, Argo, Host, Polaris, Odeon, Plus, Brokilon, Baronet, Straky na vrbě, Pistorius, Mervart, Academia, Vyšehrad, Paseka, Prostor, Kniha Zlin, Talpress, Planeta9, Epocha, MOBA, Garamond) — 220 authors.
sweeps.lesson: The category is NOT the safe-category goldmine its size suggested. 2176 records reduce to a thin canonical seam: the single largest holding is Ladislav Beran with 34 police-procedural collections (hard detective filter), and the bulk of the rest is Czech humour, literary mainstream and local memoir. The target-author pass found nearly everything of value; the frequency pass added little. For a category this large and this heterogeneous, screen by known-good author names first, and only then by imprint.
sweeps.topFind: Ted Chiang — Výdech and Příběhy vašeho života, both Host 2021. Best match to the reader's heaviest axis found in any category so far, because declaring a premise and working out its consequences IS Chiang's method rather than an obligation he might fail.
flags: Čapek's Povídky z jedné kapsy / Povídky z druhé kapsy are crime-and-detection vignettes — the hard mystery filter. Trapné povídky and Boží muka are not. Čapek is otherwise 'No signal', so do not treat a Čapek hit as uniformly proposable.
H. P. Lovecraft (3 collections) — invented mythos, but rituals and invocations are enacted on the page. Occult depiction test, same reason Divine Cities was dropped.
Roger Zelazny, Prokletý Dilvish (Straky na vrbě 2019) — sword-and-sorcery spellcasting on the page.
Šalamov, Kolymské povídky — gulag testimony, among the bleakest material in the catalogue. Bleakness is only a mild pushback, but this is the extreme end of it.
Charles Bukowski (5 titles on adult imprints) — crude sexual content is the whole register, which is the costly kind under the treatment rule.
Haruki Murakami (5 Odeon collections) — declares little so little binds him, but sexual content varies by collection and is sometimes handled crudely. Check per volume, not per author.
Agatha Christie and Jo Nesbø short fiction present — detective, hard filter.

sweeps.name: children's crossover — the literatura pro děti a mládež heading, in full
sweeps.note: Run on the reader's explicit request to screen the children's shelf for Hobbit 84 / Little Prince 82 crossover rather than for children's books. The two standing category rejects on that shelf (axis:life-phase, 2026-08-26) were deliberately looked past for this pass and still stand for the default queue.
sweeps.method: Full enumeration of the heading (68 pages at pageSize=100, pageNumber is 1-based - page 0 returns HTTP 500). Each record's MARC detailTableRows were parsed for author (field 100-a), genre/form index terms, keywords, page count and annotation. A mechanical filter dropped 4,398 records - format (leporela, komiksy, manga, workbooks, encyclopedias, audio, poetry) 2,376; under 100 pages 1,142; no page count 501; detective or romance genre terms 379 - leaving 2,381 records and 1,094 authors, of which 1,053 had never been considered. That author list was then name-reviewed in full.
sweeps.lesson: The heading sweep alone would have missed a third of the crossover canon, because the library files the best of it as adult prose: Nekonečný příběh, Momo, Sofiin svět, Alenka, Medvídek Pú, Zlodějka knih, Robinson Crusoe, Huckleberry Finn and Chlapec v pruhovaném pyžamu are all absent from literatura pro děti a mládež and were recovered only by named queries afterwards. So for THIS category the two methods are complements, not alternatives - the heading finds what is shelved as children's, the named-canon pass finds what outgrew the shelf. Second finding: the page-count filter is the cheapest picture-book discriminator there is (1,142 of 6,779 records are under 100 pages) but it also cuts exactly at Little Prince length, so anything short and canonical has to be recovered by name.
ruledOut: Age-banded 6-11 serial fiction and franchise tie-ins — now two category rows in book-rejects.jsonl rather than prose here.
Occult failures found by name: Čarodějův učeň (Krabat), Malá čarodějnice, Doručovací služba čarodějky Kiki, Howlův putující zámek, Zlobryně a sirotci — all title-level reject rows.

Watership Down is NOT held: the only Richard Adams record is Příběhy z Kamenitého vrchu (Mladá fronta 1998), which is the Tales from Watership Down sequel. Recorded because it is the obvious title to look for and the obvious wrong conclusion to draw.

Not held at all, checked by name: Jáma (Holes), Kouzelná mýtnice (The Phantom Tollbooth), Most do země Terabithia, Skellig, the Prydain cycle, the Moomin novels (only Neviditelné dítě, Argo 2025, and the comics), Tajná zahrada.

The 353-record 'dobrodružné romány' heading and the 1,045-record 'romány pro děti a mládež' heading, which overlap this one but are not subsets of it.

sweeps.scope: Terry Pratchett, complete author holding; assessed for the Discworld series only
sweeps.lesson: Talpress publishes Discworld as TWO-NOVEL OMNIBUS volumes, and MARC 245 puts the second novel in $b, so the catalogue `name` is one title while `subtitle` is a DIFFERENT novel. Nine records collapse eighteen novels this way. A title-string join therefore misses half the series - 'Mali bohove' and 'Tezke melodicno' are reachable only as the second half of a volume named after another book. Read `subtitle` and `Udaje o edici` (which carries both numbers, e.g. '13, 14') before concluding a volume is not held. Second: the CZECH series numbering is NOT the English canon numbering - the catalogue calls Going Postal 30 where the English series calls it 33, because the Czech run excludes the Tiffany books and the Science of Discworld volumes. Use the catalogue's own number and name the English title beside it. Third, a method error worth more than a book: detailTableRows is a list of {columns:[{content:label},{content:htmlValue}]}, NOT {label,value} - a parser using label/value keys silently returns nothing at all, which is what happened on the first pass here and made 52 records look annotation-free when 40 of them carry a real Czech plot summary.
sweeps.ruledOut: Occult, 7 titles plus a sub-series row: Discworld's witches are drawn from documented English folk witchcraft and their rites are performed on the page, failing both the source and the depiction test - the Harry Potter 51 objection, and the reader's own words were that magic drawn from real-world historical witchcraft is not fine. Detective, 4 titles: the Watch volumes whose engine is a murder or theft inquiry, one confirmed by the library's own annotation ('Kdo vrazdi neskodne starce? ... vystopovat vraha'). Opening, 2 titles: The Light Fantastic and the 1+2 omnibus, both requiring the volume already abandoned at 30. Category, 1 row: the board game, the Cabell biography, the encyclopedia foreword, the cat humour book and Science of Discworld IV are not novels.
sweeps.notYetSwept: The Pratchett NON-Discworld holdings, deliberately out of scope because the request was the Discworld series: 'Dlouha zeme' and 'Dlouha valka' (with Stephen Baxter, Talpress 2013 and 2014) are the strongest untouched axis match in this author - one declared premise, stepping sideways into an unbounded chain of parallel Earths, with the annotation describing consequences being worked out; 'Filuta' (Dodger, 2016); and the story collections 'Jednim tahem pera' (Kniha Zlin 2024) and 'Mrknuti obrazovky' (2021). NOT held by this library and so unreachable: Zlodej casu, Nocni hlidka, Buch!, Neviditelni akademici, Posledni hrdina, and the remaining Tiffany Aching volumes.

preModelDrop.fix: All publisher tokens now match at a word boundary via pub_has(); short tokens are listed in _BOUNDARY. Title regexes narrowed to investigation and courtship words rather than nouns that merely appear in them.

romanceSplit.why: 1,612 romance-only works, but 1,520 of them were classed by IMPRINT alone - and the imprints were Ikar (737 records), Motto (328) and Alpress (384), which are broad trade houses, not category-romance publishers. Motto carries Neomillnerova's fantasy and Klevisova's crime; Ikar carries travel guides and paranormal. Dropping them would have repeated the Baronet/Dobrovsky mistake I had already fixed once: a house that also publishes canon must WEIGHT, never CLASS.
romanceSplit.resolution: ROMANCE_PUB_STRICT narrowed to harlequin + cosmopolis. Two grades now: romance-hi (category imprint, or a romance title AND a broad-commercial house corroborating) is dropped; romance-maybe (title regex firing alone - the case that misread Komensky's raj SRDCE) keeps model tokens.
romanceSplit.effect: Only 241 works dropped as romance-hi, not 1,520. 1,449 moved back into the queue as unknown. Net queue change is roughly flat - the saving was illusory and unsafe.

coverage.triageGap: book-triage.jsonl only contains records from BULK sweeps. Titles found by targeted single queries bypassed tier 1 entirely - Hirsi Ali's Rebelka and Kacirka are in book-cache.json but have no triage row, and the 'Rebelka' rows in triage are three different books by McGoldrick, Yarros and Reid. Consequence: two of the holdout labels used earlier were title collisions (Promena/Roberts-vs-Kafka, Rebelka/Yarros-vs-Hirsi Ali), so the backtest numbers were slightly pessimistic. Fix: have /book-screen write a triage row for every targeted find too, not just sweep output.

bugsFound: TITLE-LEVEL REJECTS WERE INERT DATA. rejected_authors() read only level author and series, so nothing ever read a title row. Americti bohove had been rejected and still came back a 5 from two separate model runs. triage.py now has rejected_titles(), and the rejected class went 286 -> 307 rows the moment it was added.

A WORK RE-PUBLISHED UNDER A DIFFERENT CZECH TITLE was invisible to that join. Jota titled the whole Chaos Walking trilogy 'Chaos' where Slovart used per-volume titles, so a book already at tier 2 came back as a score-5 novelty. czTitleAliases now exists and triage.py reads it.

26 PUBLISHER NEEDLES COULD NEVER MATCH. pub_has() and pub_tier() are fed a de-accented string but the token lists were written with diacritics, so mlada fronta, knizni klub, dobrovsky, lidove nakladatelstvi, cs. spisovatel, vysehrad, navrat, portal and the entire canon-era imprint bonus had never fired. Fixed; the rank backtest went from top 14.6% to top 12.7% median. It had failed SAFE - a class that never fires leaves a row in the queue - but it flattened the ranking.

PORTAL IS NOT A CHILDREN'S PUBLISHER. Fixing the line above put 'portal' live in KIDS_PUB and it immediately classed 120 adult psychology and pedagogy titles as children's books, including the Sacks volume promoted in this very batch. noRepeatGuarantee.asked: 2026-08-26 — is the same title evaluated only once, and is 'already promoted' recorded in book-ai-rank.jsonl?
noRepeatGuarantee.answerWas: No to both. Both are now fixed; this block records what was actually wrong.

oneVerdictPerWhat.was: A verdict is keyed on workkey(title, author) using the strings THE CATALOGUE writes, so the guarantee was 'one verdict per string pair', not 'one verdict per book'. Records collapse into works, editions do not collapse across spellings.
oneVerdictPerWhat.measured: 20 exact duplicate groups (same normalised title AND same de-feminised surname) each got two verdicts - 0.2% of an 11,602-row store, so the token waste is negligible. 15 of those survive a volume-number filter as genuine same-book pairs. Examples: Tolkien under 'J.R.R.' and 'John Ronald Reuel', Jana Eyrova vs Jane Eyrova, Harry Potter a tajemna komnata vs Harry Potter tajemna komnata.
oneVerdictPerWhat.theRealFinding: Where the model saw the same book twice it DISAGREED WITH ITSELF in 3 of 20 cases, mean 1.7 points, max 2 - and the two Tajemna komnata records came out 5 and 1. That is the only measurement of single-verdict noise there is, and it means the >=4 cutoff is soft at its boundary: a work at 3 may be a 4 that got unlucky. Worth far more than the 0.2% of wasted tokens.
oneVerdictPerWhat.fix: `python tools/ai_rank.py dupes` reports candidate pairs. It REPORTS AND NEVER MERGES, on purpose: Letopisy kralovske komory V and VI are 96% similar and are different books, as are Zapisnik alkoholicky / nealkoholicky and Rekni ano / ne vevodovi. Pairs differing only by a volume number are suppressed, without which 47 of 62 rows were Egyptanky 1-7 and Toulky ceskou minulosti 6-8.
oneVerdictPerWhat.stillOpen: Nothing collapses the variant keys automatically, so a duplicate can still be promoted twice by hand. The dupes report is the guard, and it has to actually be run.

promotionMarker.was: NOT recorded anywhere in book-ai-rank.jsonl. Verdict rows carried only k, s, w, m, pd, at. 109 of 113 tier-2 works had a live verdict row with nothing saying they were finished.
promotionMarker.whyThatMattered: The exclusion was computed at batch time from book-triage.jsonl's `next: promoted` field, which is itself derived from a TITLE-STRING JOIN against this file. That made one string comparison the single point of failure for the entire no-repeat guarantee, and it failed three separate times on 2026-08-26: exact-string casing, a work re-published under another Czech title, and a title-level reject nothing read. book-triage.jsonl is also regenerable only from the temp pulls, which do not survive a session - it was destroyed once that day, which would have re-exposed all 113 promoted books.
promotionMarker.fix: `python tools/ai_rank.py seal` writes `done: <cacheKey>` onto the verdict of every work that reached tier 2, and creates a marker row for the 4 tier-2 works no model ever scored. cmd_batches now checks `done` as well as `skip`. `done` is a fact about the work, not about the prompt, so a digest change does not clear it. RUN IT AFTER EVERY PROMOTION - 113 works sealed 2026-08-26.
promotionMarker.markerRowsHaveNoScore: Deliberate. Writing s:0 on them put fake zeroes into the distribution and made the dupes report claim Siddhartha scored '(0) ~ (5), disagrees'.

rankPromptV3Experiment.outcome: BUILT, RUN OVER THE WHOLE CORPUS, MEASURED, REVERTED. v2 is live again.
rankPromptV3Experiment.cost: ~1.5M tokens, 23 Haiku agents, 10,782 verdicts merged (190 unparseable)

whyReverted.recallAt4: 56% against v2's 77%, on a 112-work holdout of tier-2 works that seal had excluded from the run, so genuinely unseen.
whyReverted.lostOutright: 11 of 64 known-good works scored 1 or 2, which is not a queue position - Rebelka (est 82, the strongest non-fiction match in the library), Pul krale 78, Prezila jsem cinsky gulag 76, Slysim te vsude 72, Jursky park 72, Promena 70, Naslouchej nozi 70, Fantasticke povidky 70, Cizinec 68.
whyReverted.precision: 50% of known RECORDED-LOW works also scored >=4, so the smaller queue was not a cleaner one.

keepFromIt.annotationInTheInput: THE BIG WIN, keep it. Over 10,782 v3 verdicts, a row WITH a catalogue annotation scored >=4 11.1% of the time against 2.4% without - 4.6x. Named an idea 15.1% vs 6.9%. Recognised 7.5% vs 3.7%. Coverage 91% at record level, 59% of the ranking population, and it skews to recent acquisitions: 10% of 1980s works have one against 71% of 2010s, so it helps least exactly where the canon is.
keepFromIt.recFlag: Keep. It exposed what v2 hid: asked directly, the model recognises only 6% of the corpus, while 42% of v2 verdicts were non-3 and thereby implied recognition. Most of v2's confident scores were not based on knowing the book. On known-good works rec ran 34% against 6% corpus-wide, so it carries signal - but that is the canonicity bias again, since canonical books are both recognisable and good.

dropFromIt.ideaFlag: MEASURED USELESS. 70% of known-good works had a nameable idea against 71% of known-low - one point in the wrong direction. This flag was the entire justification for choosing a binary field over a 0-10 scale, on the argument that a flag is auditable and a 7-against-9 is not. The argument was sound and the flag still does not work. Do not quote it as an ordering signal.
dropFromIt.reframingOf3: PRIME SUSPECT for the recall collapse. v3 said a 3 no longer means 'did not recognise' while also demanding an honest rec flag; everything then collapsed toward the middle. The 3-bucket grew 58% -> 72%, 1s and 2s shrank 3,550 -> 2,210, and >=4 shrank 1,310 -> 813. Honesty pressure plus a widened middle makes a model that will not commit.

rankPromptV3Experiment.v4: v2's instructions and scale unchanged, PLUS the annotation in the input and the rec flag in the output. No idea flag, no reframing of 3. Measure against the same 113-work holdout BEFORE it touches the live store - that is the step this run skipped, and it cost 1.5M tokens to find out.
rankPromptV3Experiment.mechanism: tools/ai_rank.py appends the annotation only when the live prompt BODY contains the word 'annotation', so v2 rows stay at title/author/publisher/year and its stored verdicts stay valid. The v3 prompt and its holdout verdicts are kept at tools/ai-rank-prompt-v3.md.
rankPromptV3Experiment.sealWorkedButHidTheHoldout: seal correctly kept all 113 promoted works out of the run. That also removed the only available holdout, so the measurement needed a separate 113-work pass afterwards. Next time run the holdout FIRST, on one batch, before spending the corpus.

sonnetPromotion.design: One Sonnet agent does the WHOLE tier-2 job per book: research it on the web, verify a Czech print route against the catalogue API, derive est/leanedOn/risks/why, emit one JSON file. Contract in tools/promote-prompt.md, tooling in tools/promote.py. enAudio deliberately out of scope for this pass.

twoStructuralRules.agentsNeverWriteSharedFiles: Each writes <key>.json to a staging dir and `absorb` is the only writer of book-cache.json / book-estimates.jsonl / book-media.json. Parallel promotions doing read-modify-write on one JSON file lose work silently and without a readable diff.
twoStructuralRules.agentsNeverReadTheEstimates: Blind to book-estimates.jsonl and book-cache.json. Does double duty: an estimate argued from another CANDIDATE is a guess anchored to a guess and crossrefs.py fails on it, and a holdout is only a measurement if the answer was not on disk in front of the model.

holdoutMeasured.method: 8 books that already had a hand-derived est, spanning 52-62 to 80-88, both sides of the 68 propose/record line. Agents could not see the answers.
holdoutMeasured.verdictFlips: 2 of 8 (25%) - the number that decides usability
holdoutMeasured.leanedOnAgreement: 6 of 8 shared an axis with the hand estimate
holdoutMeasured.predictedVsActual: The pre-registered worry was that a +/-5 point error flips 45% of books, because 46% of estimates sit within 5 points of the boundary. Actual flip rate 25%, so better than the worst case but not negligible.
holdoutMeasured.theTwoFlips: 2001 Vesmirna odysea: model 64-74 against hand 72-82. The model weighted the unrootable cast and the deliberately unexplained final act harder than the hand estimate did, and it is arguably MORE right - both were named as deductions by hand and then under-applied. Jana Eyrova: model 78-88 against hand 64-74, +14, the one clear miss. The model leaned on the rootable first-person narrator and moral autonomy and did not price the sustained romance middle or the Moor House stall; 78-88 would put a Victorian romance near the top of the log, which the profile does not support.
holdoutMeasured.bias: mean +2 - the model is slightly generous. Worth a nudge in the next prompt revision.

sonnetPromotion.verdict: USABLE WITH GUARDRAILS at n=8, which is a thin sample. (1) Spot-audit anything with est low >= 80, because a false high there becomes the next proposal. (2) A false low is recoverable - the book still lands in the database with a real range and can be revisited - so the asymmetry favours letting it run. (3) Unlike the ranking step, every output carries sourced reasoning in `why`, so an audit is reading one paragraph rather than re-deriving the book.
sonnetPromotion.absorbRefusals: Validates genre/form against fixed sets, REQUIRES a full 36-char record uuid (the truncation that broke 54 links), requires non-empty `sources`, checks leanedOn/risks are a subset of deps, and holds any confidence:low file unless --force-low. It fills the six mandatory dep axes and the author id itself so a model cannot omit them, and stamps current revs so an estimate is never born stale. Verified on the holdout: all 8 correctly refused with 'key already in book-cache.json' and nothing was written.

rankPromptV4Holdout.prompt: tools/ai-rank-prompt-v4.md — v2's body and scale VERBATIM, plus the catalogue annotation in the input and a rec flag in the output. No idea flag, no reframing of 3, which were v3's two losing changes.
rankPromptV4Holdout.design: 328 tier-2 works with a hand-derived est and a joinable annotation, scored by one Haiku agent that could not see the est. Matched baseline for free: every one of them already carried a v2 verdict on disk, so the same works were measured under both prompts with one variable changed. Ground truth: est low >= 68 = the book was judged worth proposing, which is what a >=4 is meant to catch. This is the holdout-FIRST step the v3 run skipped.
rankPromptV4Holdout.populationCorrection: Reported on 264 works, not 328. The 32 children's-crossover promotions were excluded because their est was derived under a rubric where children's register is GRADED, while both rankers treat children's books as a hard 1 - and because v2 never scored them at all, so leaving them in penalised v2 for silence and v4 for obeying its own rules. Never compare two prompts on a population only one of them was run over.
rankPromptV4Holdout.annotationEffect: Confirmed and larger than v3 measured it: of the holdout rows WITH an annotation 37% scored >=4, against 6% of rows without - 6.2x, where v3 measured 4.6x. rec=1 came back on 34% of the holdout against ~6% corpus-wide, which is the canonicity of the promoted set rather than a prompt effect.
rankPromptV4Holdout.verdict: v4 FAILS the pre-registered criterion, which was to beat v2's 77% recall at >=4. It gets 44%. But the same run shows the criterion was measuring the wrong thing: on this matched population v2's recall of 85% comes with a 92% false-positive rate, precision 35% and a known-good/known-low mean spread of +0.12 - v2 at >=4 is not a shortlist, it is very nearly 'score everything 4'. That is the mechanism behind the 857-work >=4 pile nobody will ever work through.
rankPromptV4Holdout.whyRecallFell: The annotation removes a free ride. v2's high recall is substantially an artefact of rewarding canonicity without information, and the known-good set is heavily canonical BECAUSE it was promoted. Give the model the library's own plot summary and it stops guessing high on a famous-sounding row and starts reading the premise - which for a mediocre book reveals mediocrity. Hence false positives 92% -> 24% and recall 85% -> 44% together. So v4 is not a worse instrument, it is a differently calibrated one: v2 is high-recall/no-discrimination, v4 is medium-recall/real-discrimination.
rankPromptV4Holdout.v3ComparisonImportant: v4 does NOT reproduce the v3 catastrophe. v3 lost 11 of 64 known-good works to a 1 or a 2; v4 loses 2 of 96, exactly as many as v2 does. So dropping the idea flag and keeping v2's framing of a 3 fixed the collapse, and the earlier diagnosis of v3 was correct.
rankPromptV4Holdout.notPromoted: v4 was NOT copied over tools/ai-rank-prompt.md. Promoting it changes the live digest, marks all ~11.6k stored verdicts stale and commits ~1.3M tokens, and the pre-registered gate said no. Held for the reader's decision. The strongest single argument FOR promoting it is the >=5 bucket: 71% precision at a 2% false-positive rate against v2's 53% and 20%.

aiRankRunV4.batchSize: 500 x 23, then 400 x 2 and 44 to close the tail
aiRankRunV4.gate: See coverage.rankPromptV4Holdout. v4 failed the pre-registered recall gate and was promoted on the reader's explicit decision, because the same holdout showed v2's >=4 bucket was a 92%-false-positive pile rather than a shortlist.

vsV2._method: 11,193 works carry both a v2 and a fresh v4 verdict and are still eligible, so this is a matched comparison rather than two distributions side by side.
vsV2.queueSizeBarelyMoved: >=4 went from ~1,093 works under v2 to 1,072 under v4 - which is NOT what the holdout predicted, because the holdout's negatives were near-miss promoted books and the corpus is mostly not that.
vsV2.butTheMembershipTurnedOVER: 699 works entered the >=4 queue that v2 had at <=3, and 681 left it. Roughly two thirds of the queue is different stock at the same size. Combined with the holdout's precision figures (51% vs 35% at >=4, 71% vs 53% at >=5) that swap is the return on the run.
vsV2.blindBucketPayoff: Of the 6,851 works v2 had parked at 3 having seen only title/author/publisher/year, 581 moved to >=4 once the annotation was fed - 8.5%.
vsV2.annotationEffectAtCorpusScale: 12.9% of annotated rows scored >=4 against 2.0% of unannotated - 6.5x, which reproduces the holdout's 6.2x and v3's 4.6x on a third population.
vsV2.recognition: rec=1 on 935 of 12,382 works = 7.6% (6.7% of annotated rows, 3.6% of unannotated). Confirms the v3 finding that the model knows ~6% of this corpus and that v2's confident scores were mostly not based on knowing the book.

joinDefectsSurfaced: A TITLE-LEVEL REJECT CAN BE BYPASSED BY AN AUTHOR-STRING VARIANT, and this is the first time the known 'one verdict per string pair, not per book' limit has had a correctness consequence rather than just wasting tokens. Howluv putujici zamek exists under two workkeys because two slices spell the author differently: 'Diana Wynne Jonesova' from responsibilityStatement and 'Jones, Diana Wynne' from MARC 100-a. The reject rejected the second key correctly and the first was sent to the model and came back a 5. Same shape on Letni valka. FIX DIRECTION: match rejects on the normalised TITLE alone as well as on the pair, or collapse variant author keys - the dupes report already finds these pairs and deliberately never merges them.

AN EXCLUSION THAT LIVES ONLY IN PROSE IS STILL INVISIBLE, and Naomi Novik was the live example: 'Avoid' in the Authors table since 2026-08-26 with no reject row, so rejected_authors() had no 'novik' at all and her Letni valka scored 5. Row added 2026-08-27. This was already recorded as a lesson and it recurred anyway, which argues for a check that greps the Authors table for Avoid rows with no matching reject line.

load_works()'s 'one usable edition rescues the work' rule is right for edition problems and wrong for taste rejects: an audio-only record should not kill a work that also exists in print, but a title-level reject should kill it whatever edition it is held in.
aiRankRunV4.interAgentVariance: LARGE, and it is a property of the run rather than of the books. The batches are emitted best-first by metadata rank, so the >=4 share should fall monotonically across batch numbers. It does not: batch 006 returned 0 fours out of 500 and batch 019 returned 125 of 500, batch 018 returned 496 threes out of 500 while batch 004 returned 116 fours. So a work's score partly reflects which agent happened to read it. The right guard is what the 2026-08-26 duplicate study already implies - the >=4 cutoff is soft at its boundary - and the practical consequence is that a 3 must never be read as a no.

fivesPromotionV4.input: the 34 works the v4 corpus run scored 5; 3 were already tier 2 or came from the children's crossover rubric, leaving 31 queued
fivesPromotionV4.method: tools/promote.py batch --min-score 5 --per 12 (3 batches), one Sonnet agent per batch under tools/promote-prompt.md, staged per-book JSON, absorb the only writer. Access routes were precomputed so no agent queried the catalogue.
fivesPromotionV4._outcome: 26 estimates, 3 title-level rejects (Muz z Vysokeho zamku - I Ching divination enacted on the page; Nocni cirkus; Sire Sargasove more - Christophine's obeah shown to work), 2 retracted for having been rejected already, 2 refused by crossrefs and re-absorbed after the offending citation was removed. NOTHING came back with an est floor >= 80, so the spot-audit the +2 generosity bias calls for had nothing to check.
fivesPromotionV4.theHeadline: A score of 5 from the ranker is NOT a prediction, and this run is the proof. Of 26 estimates only 5 reached a floor of 70 - Eleanor se ma vazne skvele 74-84, Posledni jednorozec 72-82, Kral byvaly a kral budouci 72-82, Soumrak dne 70-80, Pycha a premlouvani 70-80 - and 7 landed below 60, with Sogun at 30-40 on the infidelity filter and Tess z d'Urbervillu at 48-60. The canonicity the ranker rewards is orthogonal to this reader's axes, exactly as the holdout's 71% precision at >=5 predicted: about a fifth of the bucket was never going to survive contact with the profile.
fivesPromotionV4.bestFinds: Eleanor se ma vazne skvele (Honeyman, Plus 2017) is the only one that clears the propose line comfortably. Posledni jednorozec and Kral byvaly a kral budouci are the strongest of the fantasy canon entries; Soumrak dne and Pycha a premlouvani are motive-driven literary picks. Pycha a premlouvani is Persuasion, genuinely unread - it only LOOKED already-read because the read join is by surname and Pride and Prejudice 75 is now in the log.
fivesPromotionV4.gateFailureFound: THE REJECT GATE WAS DEAD FOR ACCENTED TITLES AND BLIND TO AUTHOR-LEVEL ROWS, and this run is how it surfaced: Howluv putujici zamek and Letni valka were both rejected on the occult filter earlier the same day, were queued anyway, were researched and estimated by an agent, and were absorbed - so the database briefly held a reject row and an est for one book, the exact state absorb's guard exists to prevent. Four separate causes, all now fixed in already_decided() and _decided(): (1) the reject entity was lowercased but never de-accented while both callers compare against deacc(), so EVERY Czech title-level reject was inert - masked only because the earlier rows happened to be written ASCII-only; (2) author-level and series-level rows were skipped by `if level != 'title': continue`, so an author reject excluded nothing; (3) an entity written `Czech title (Original Title)` was indexed whole and matched neither half, which triage.py had handled since 2026-08-26 and this module never did; (4) eszett survives NFKD and slug() turned Preussler into `preu-ler`, so authorid could not match the same author spelled without it. After the fix all seven test cases resolve correctly, including the series-level Jefferson rows via a prefix match scoped by author.
fivesPromotionV4.secondGateFailure: absorb did not write the `audience` facet, because that field was added hours earlier and the promotion pipeline predates it - so 26 new rows were unfilterable in the viewer. promote.py now writes it, optional on the staged file and defaulted to adult/`default`, and the 26 were backfilled. LESSON: adding a required cache field means teaching every writer of that file, not just the reader of it.

tier4PromotionRun1.input: the first 100 works, best-first, of the 1,038 the v4 corpus run scored 4. The 5s were already promoted (coverage.fivesPromotionV4), so this is the first pass into the bucket below them.

tier4PromotionRun1.theHeadline: 16 of 90 estimates reached the 68 propose line and 14 reached a floor of 70 - so the score-4 bucket is roughly as productive per book as the 5s were (5 of 26 at a floor of 70), at a fifth of the hit rate the bucket's size suggests. 55 of the 90 wrote the [58,68] C-low default, which is the gate working, not the agents giving up.
tier4PromotionRun1.bestFinds: Andelin popel 76-86 (memoir-form, the axis Seeking Allah and Son of Hamas score on), Normalni lidi 76-86, Dve mista na slunci 76-85, Prestupni stanice 76-85 (Simak), Vyhodme ho z kola ven 73-82 (Kesey), then Hukot casu / Intermezzo / Kosmonaut z Cech / Mladej Mungo at 72-82.
tier4PromotionRun1.rejects: 10 title-level: 8 occult (a rite enacted on the page - Flamel-series invocation, a witch's divination, shamanistic ancestor prayer, coffee-ground fortune telling shown to work, an invented death-god with a praying priesthood, fire divination), 1 detective (Posel - the momentum is the whodunnit of who sends the cards), 1 infidelity-as-premise (Nas Coney Island - a 25-year affair between two married people IS the book).

The 0-of-15 batch was almost pure series volumes and anthologies so composition explains it, but the spread is the same one the v4 ranking run measured and it is not shrinking.
tier4PromotionRun1.leanedOnEmptyFailure: One agent left leanedOn AND risks empty on 11 of its 15 files - 11 of the 17 refusals, and 19% of all C-low exits in the run. The contract never said the field survives an early exit, and at C the number is carried by the doubt rather than by a positive axis, so 'nothing to lean on' is a reading an agent can reach honestly. Fixed in tools/promote-prompt.md gate 3 rather than by hand-filling the files: the agents transcribed the axis their own why already argued.
tier4PromotionRun1.seriesCollapseFound: The catalogue files a series under the bare series title in MARC 245 $a with the volume in $n/$p, so every volume shares one work key and one annotation. Hit 2 of these 100. Sirotcinec slecny Peregrinove was the bad one: the work row collapses volumes two to six, its annotation described a later volume's Noor Pradesh arc, and fetch-editions.py had routed it to a 2023 companion GUIDEBOOK because that is the newest print edition of the collapsed row. Previtem snadno a rychle links to volume three while the estimate argues volume two; flagged rather than re-researched, since it is a [58,68] row that will never be proposed. All 89 routed rows were checked against api/records/<uuid>.

tier4PromotionRun1.spend: Measured: 966k subagent tokens over the 7 promotion batches, plus 53k over the 5 resumed agents that fixed the 17 refusals, so 1.02M for 100 books = 10.2k/book against the 7.5k/book the per=15 model predicts. Gate spend held everywhere except C: 24 of 59 C exits spent 2 sources against a budget of 1 (mean 1.41), while B-occult came in at 1.88 of 4 and D-full at 2.58 of 6 - so the C overspend is the one budget still inverted, exactly as it was on 2026-08-26.
tier4PromotionRun1.remainingInBucket: 822 works, measured 2026-08-27 after seal - NOT 938. The bucket holds 1,972 works at score 4, but 819 are triage-skip (already read, or an author/series already rejected), 202 are sealed done and 21 are decided by another channel. 822 is the live queueable count, and it is the only one worth quoting: the raw bucket size overstates the work by 58%.

twoRulings.newHardFilter: Sex as the plot. Reader's words: reject "when the plot is severely/mainly about sexual behavior/relationship". Premise test, same shape as the infidelity filter - remove the sex and there is no book. NOT about explicitness, NOT a marriage rule. Filter id axis:sexual-content. Sixth hard filter.
twoRulings.gradedAxisCorrected: The reader overruled the 2026-08-22 "crudeness of treatment, not quantity" wording: volume, explicitness and crudeness ALL cost, each on its own, and they compound. The old wording's specific error was citing Red Rising 95 as PROOF that volume is free - Red Rising is simply low on all three dimensions and so was barely docked. A book that never incurred a penalty is not evidence the penalty does not exist. Fourth revision of this axis.

sexAxisRuleChange.onlyOccasional: Resolved a knock-on: "only occasional" used to be VOID as an argument. Under the correction low volume is genuine mitigation - that is what makes volume a dimension - so it is now mitigation, never clearance, and never an argument for eligibility.

propagation.theRuleHeldItsShape: The filter is narrow and the agents kept it narrow. The Lot Lands trilogy, Futu.re and It's Me Eddie all carry pervasive, graphic, crude content and were NOT blocked, because their plots survive removing the sex - they took the deduction instead. Kundera split three ways under one agent: Laughable Loves and Slowness blocked, Identity held at 60-70 because its theme is desire while its plot is the anonymous letters. plavec-ve-tme held at 70-80, the boundary case flagged to the reader before the scope was chosen.
propagation.usefulNegative: prevorstvi-u-pomerancovniku held at 66-76 even though its why used the overruled Red Rising phrasing: the agent checked sources instead of pattern-matching the wording and found the book genuinely light on all three dimensions. the-blade-itself held because its why had already voided the "only occasional" argument before the rule changed. Wrong reasoning and wrong conclusion are not the same defect.
propagation.auditTrail: Every one of the 75 rows now carries sexualProfile {volume, explicitness, crudeness, isThePlot}, so the three dimensions are auditable data rather than prose and the next revision of this axis has something to check against.

unrankedNotThree.ruling: Reader: "Not recognized should not be 3, but NaN." An unrecognised verdict has NO score - it is unranked, not a middling 3.
unrankedNotThree.whyItMattered: `rec` has been stored since v3 but every consumer read `s` alone, so "I do not know this book" and "I know it and it is middling" both presented as 3. The file's own _bucket3 note asserted the opposite of the truth - that a v3+ 3 means the model could see the book and could not call it - and that note misled a reading of the corpus earlier the same day.
unrankedNotThree.theData: At score 3, 10,425 of 10,821 verdicts carry rec=0 - the bucket is 96% unrecognised works. Under v2 a 3 also meant unrecognised, at 58% of all verdicts. So a 3 has never been a judgement under either prompt.
unrankedNotThree.measuredOnRealOutcomes: Validated against the 100 books promoted from the score-4 bucket the same day, which is the only test available: a RECOGNISED 4 reached the 68 propose line 7 times in 25 (28%), an unrecognised 4 six times in 67 (9%). 3.1x, Fisher exact two-tailed p = 0.038. Rejects ran 4% against 12%, and 43 of the 67 unrecognised books wrote the [58,68] C-low default. So the conflation was not merely untidy - 73 of those 100 books were unrecognised, and they converted at a third of the rate.
unrankedNotThree.queueEffect: The live queue at >= 4 falls from 822 works to 226. The other 596 are unranked and move to the re-rank pool, not the bin.
unrankedNotThree.implementation: tools/ai_rank.py ranked(r) returns None when rec is falsy; `status` reports UNRANKED separately and prints what those rows would have counted as. promote.py eligible_score() gates queue and batch on it, with --include-unranked as the escape hatch for a run that deliberately samples them. `s` is still stored, because it is the model's raw output and this is a reading defect, not a data defect.
unrankedNotThree.notFixedInThePrompt: Deliberate. Making the model emit no score for rec=0 would change tools/ai-rank-prompt.md, hence its digest, hence re-send all 12,382 verdicts for ~1.3M tokens - to recover information already sitting in the file.
unrankedNotThree.openGap: The no-repeat guarantee is keyed on the PROMPT digest, not on the input. A work whose annotation arrives after its verdict is never re-sent even though the evidence changed, so re-ranking newly-annotated works needs a targeted `pd` clear on exactly those rows.

_genre: sf | fantasy | litfic | historical | testimony | allegory | thriller. A fact about the book, so it lives here and not in book-estimates.jsonl. One value; when a book straddles two, pick what a reader looking for that shelf would expect and let `flags` carry the nuance.
_form: novel | novella | stories | nonfiction. Orthogonal to genre and kept separate on purpose: Chiang's Vydech and Saki's collection are both `stories` and share nothing else. `stories` covers single-author collections and anthologies alike - the unit catalogued is the volume.
_aliases: czTitleAliases: other Czech titles the same WORK is catalogued under. The promoted-title join in tools/triage.py reads these, so a second edition published under a different name stops coming back as an unscreened find. Jota titled the whole Chaos Walking trilogy 'Chaos' where Slovart used per-volume titles, and that is how it re-entered the queue as a score-5 novelty.
_audience: Who the EDITION was published for, and a fact like genre and form - not a verdict on whether an adult should read it, which is axis:childrens in book-estimates.jsonl. adult | ya | childrens. `audienceSource` says how it was got: katalog = the library's own zanr/forma index term (publikace pro deti / pro mladez / literatura young adult), hand = assigned from the edition and imprint because that record carries no term, default = nothing known and adult is the assumption, NOT a finding. Added 2026-08-27 so the children's shelf is filterable in the viewer without collapsing genre.
_prereq: Reading-order links, added 2026-08-31 because they existed only as prose and nothing could join on them. A list of {ref, kind, need, note}. `ref` is a book-cache key, a books-read.md slug, a book-rejects.jsonl entity, or a parenthesised description when the predecessor is not held at all. `kind` = candidate | read | rejected | absent. `need` = hard when the book cannot be read without it (plot continues, or the lead or premise is introduced there and assumed rather than re-established) | soft when it merely helps. THE INHERITANCE RULE KEYS ON THIS FIELD: a hard prereq that is excluded excludes this book too; a soft one does not. The unit is dependency, never the series - Mort 83 is volume four of a series whose volume one was abandoned at 30, and it is the best Pratchett result in the log. `inherits: false` marks a hard prereq that is excluded but does NOT propagate - the only case so far is a predecessor rejected on `access`. Recorded as a field rather than as prose so a consistency check can see the exception instead of reporting it forever.
